This crusader lord ruled Antioch and Transjordan by right of marriage, and once tortured the Latin Patriarch of Antioch over unpaid funds before raiding Byzantine Cyprus — who was he?
Raynald of Châtillon: Crusader and military leader (1125–1187)
The longest-serving U.S. secretary of defense, this Cold War-era Pentagon chief championed systems analysis and escalated American involvement in the Vietnam War — who was he?
Robert McNamara: American businessman and government official (1916–2009)
Born in London to a Pakistani family, this Labour politician served as MP for Tooting before becoming the third mayor of London in 2016?
Sadiq Khan: Mayor of London since 2016. Sir Sadiq Aman Khan (born 8 October 1970) is a British politician serving as the third and current strategic authority mayor for London since 2016.
Before becoming Australia's 30th prime minister in 2018, this politician ran Tourism Australia and served as the New South Wales Liberal Party's state director — who is he?
Scott Morrison: Prime Minister of Australia from 2018 to 2022.
Known by the honorific Bangabandhu, this founding president of Bangladesh was assassinated in a 1975 coup after leading the country since 1972 — who is he?
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman: Bangladeshi revolutionary and statesman (1920–1975)
After finding fame as Tulsi in India's most-watched soap opera, this actress-turned-politician joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2003 and later held roles in India's Union Cabinet — who is she?
Smriti Irani: Indian actress and politician (born 1976)

This East African Muslim state, ruled by a hereditary sultan from 1856 to 1964, once controlled a coastal strip of Kenya before losing it and eventually being overthrown by revolutionaries — what was it called?
Sultanate of Zanzibar: 1856–1964 East African Muslim state. It was also involved in the shortest war in history, the Anglo-Zanzibar War, which lasted 38 minutes on the morning of 27 August 1896.
This biblical figure, son of Nahor, is best known as the father of the patriarch Abraham in the Book of Genesis — who is he?
Terah: Figure in the Hebrew Bible; son of Nahor.

The third son of Japan's founding Edo-period shōgun, this samurai ruled as the second shōgun of that dynasty from 1605 until his 1623 abdication, and became grandfather to Empress Meishō — who was he?
Tokugawa Hidetada: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1605 to 1623.
A trained physician who served as Germany's Defence Minister under Angela Merkel, she has led the European Commission since 2019 — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen: President of the European Commission since 2019. Von der Leyen was born and raised in Brussels, Belgium, to German parents.
Canonized as a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches, this Rurik dynasty ruler seized Kiev with a Varangian army in 978 after his brothers' deadly feud — who is he?
Vladimir the Great: Grand Prince of Kiev from 978 to 1015.
Crowned King of Prussia in 1861, this Hohenzollern monarch became the first emperor of a unified Germany a decade later — who was he?
Wilhelm I: German Emperor from 1871 to 1888.
Known by his initials, this Indian politician served as chief minister of Andhra Pradesh for two terms before dying in a 2009 helicopter crash over a forest — who was he?
Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy: Chief minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Yeduguri Sandinti Rajasekhara Reddy (8 July 1949 – 2 September 2009), popularly known as YSR, was an Indian politician.
From Chittagong in March 1971 he broadcast his nation's declaration of independence; he later rose to become its sixth president and is remembered there as the 'Martyr President.' Which leader?
Ziaur Rahman: President of Bangladesh from 1977 to 1981.
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these four came first?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Frank Oppenheimer is a physicist. The younger brother of renowned physicist J.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Émilie du Châtelet is a mathematician. It circulated widely, generated heated debates, and was translated into German and Italian in 1743.
What is the atomic number of Hassium?
Hassium: Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
What is the atomic number of Krypton?
Krypton: Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.
In what year was Alfred Nobel born?
Alfred Nobel: Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( noh-BEL; Swedish: [ˈǎlːfrɛd nʊˈbɛlː]; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
In what year was Kitty Oppenheimer born?
Kitty Oppenheimer: Robert Oppenheimer, the director of the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II.
In what year was John Maynard Keynes born?
John Maynard Keynes: Keynes was educated at King's College at the University of Cambridge, where he graduated in 1904 with a B.A. in mathematics.
In what year did Thales of Miletus die?
Thales of Miletus: Thales of Miletus ( THAY-leez; Ancient Greek: Θαλῆς; c. 626/623 – c. 548/545 BC) was an Ancient Greek pre-Socratic philosopher from Miletus in Ionia, Asia Minor.
In what year did Ernest Rutherford die?
Ernest Rutherford: Together with Thomas Royds, Rutherford is credited with proving that alpha radiation is composed of helium nuclei.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium: Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 from?

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Soviet Union. The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 (Russian: Микоян и Гуревич МиГ-19; NATO reporting name: Farmer) is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Pyxis?
Pyxis: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pyxis is a small and faint constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Neodymium?
Neodymium: Carl Auer von Welsbach. Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
Who is credited with discovering TON 618?
Who is credited with discovering Thallium?
Thallium: Claude-Auguste Lamy. Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.

Produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex, this mineralocorticoid is the body's key sodium-saver, quietly governing blood pressure and potassium balance in the kidney — which hormone is it?
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.

Usually a symptom of coronary artery disease caused by atherosclerosis narrowing the arteries, this chest pain or pressure gets its name from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest' — name this condition?
Angina is chest pain or pressure, usually caused by insufficient blood flow to the heart muscle (myocardium).
This South Korean actress started as a child model in 2005 and later starred in the popular series True Beauty. Who is she?
Arrhythmia are irregularities in the heartbeat, including when it is too fast or too slow.
Nicknamed 'Red-Stockings,' this French herding dog breed hails from the plains of Central France — which breed is it?
Beauceron (French) is a herding dog breed originating from the plains of Central France.
Dermatologists call the small version of this fluid-filled skin pocket a vesicle and the larger version a bulla; its English name traces back to an Old French word for a leprous nodule. What is it?

Blister is a small pocket of body fluid (lymph, serum, plasma, blood, or pus) within the upper layers of the skin, usually caused by forceful rubbing (friction), burning, freezing, chemical exposure or infection.

More muscular and aggressive than the females of the species, this uncastrated adult male of Bos taurus has long symbolized power in religious sacrifice and features prominently in ranching and blood sports — which term describes him?
Bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).

Born in London and raised in Milan, this Italian Catholic teenager taught himself computer programming and web design to promote devotion to the Eucharist online before his death in 2006 at age 15 — who was he?
Carlo Acutis (3 May 1991 - 12 October 2006) was an English-born Italian Catholic teenager known for his devotion to the Eucharist and his use of digital media to promote Catholic devotion.
This plant-cell organelle uses chlorophyll pigments to capture sunlight and convert it into chemical energy, ultimately producing sugar via the Calvin cycle — what is it?
Chloroplast (-plahst) is a type of organelle known as a plastid that conducts photosynthesis mostly in plant and algal cells.
A true thrush of Europe, western Asia and North Africa, the male of its nominate subspecies is entirely black — and depending on latitude it may stay put or migrate. What bird is it?
Common blackbird (Turdus merula) is a species of true thrush.
A creeping vine of the gourd family that originated across Asia from India to Yunnan, this annual comes in slicing, pickling, and seedless types — what is it?
Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) is a widely-cultivated creeping vine plant in the family Cucurbitaceae that bears cylindrical to spherical fruits, used as culinary vegetables.

Lean, fast, and wedge-skulled, this medium-sized Australian canine comes in ginger, black-and-tan, or creamy white, and scientists still argue whether it's a dog, a wolf subspecies, or its own species — what is it?
Dingo is a lineage of dog found in Australia.
Despite common belief, this shocking South American fish belongs to the knifefish order and is more closely related to catfish than its name implies — what is it?
Electric eel are a genus, Electrophorus, of neotropical freshwater fish from South America in the family Gymnotidae, of which they are the only members of the subfamily Electrophorinae.
This flammable, colorless solvent smells sweetly of pear drops and shows up in glues and nail polish remover — and it's also the ester used to gently strip caffeine from tea and coffee. What is it?
Ethyl acetate (commonly abbreviated EtOAc or EA) is the organic compound with the formula CH3CO2CH2CH3, simplified to C4H8O2.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive it combines with nearly every other element except the light noble gases. What element is it (symbol F)?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.

The first person in Germany to hold a professorship dedicated to experimental physics, he is remembered for his posthumous 'waste book' notebooks and for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him. Who is he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1 July 1742 - 24 February 1799) was a German physicist, satirist, and Anglophile.
In this rapid-onset condition the immune system attacks the peripheral nerves, so weakness creeps up from the feet and hands — and about 15% of patients need a ventilator. What is it?
Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.
This genus of the mallow family includes several hundred species prized for their large, showy blooms, and is sometimes known by the alternate name rose mallow — name the genus?
Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
This medical condition occurs when the body, or a region of it, is deprived of adequate oxygen at the tissue level — what is it called?

Hypoxia (medicine) is a condition in which the body or a region of the body is deprived of an adequate oxygen supply at the tissue level. Hypoxia may be classified as either generalized, affecting the whole body, or local, affecting a region of the body.

Once found as far north as Texas's Lower Rio Grande Valley but now extirpated from the US, this slender wild cat comes in gray and red color morphs, ranging from Mexico to Argentina — what animal is it?
Jaguarundi (Herpailurus yagouaroundi); or is a wild cat native to the Americas.
A 1983 MacArthur Fellow in mathematics, this American's work on Hilbert's tenth problem proved crucial to its eventual solution — now known as the MRDP theorem. Who is she?

Julia Robinson (December 8, 1919 - July 30, 1985) was an American mathematician noted for her contributions to the fields of computability theory and computational complexity theory - most notably in decision problems.
What reddish-brown, alcohol-based tincture of opium, roughly 10% opium by weight, was historically sold without a prescription as a pain reliever and cough suppressant until the early 20th century?
Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Used since pre-Columbian times as a pack animal that can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles, which domesticated South American camelid has wool low in lanolin?
Llama (Spanish) (Lama glama) is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era.
Though it's the strongest bone in the face, this lower jawbone tends to deform with age and is prone to fractures — what is it called?

Mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower - and typically more mobile - component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).

This cluster of at least three conditions -- including high blood sugar, high triglycerides, and low 'good' cholesterol -- raises heart disease and diabetes risk in roughly a quarter of American adults. What is it called?

Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least three of the following five medical conditions: abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high serum triglycerides, and low serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
This genus of edible sac fungi has a honeycomb-like cap of ridges and pits, is prized in French and Catalan cooking, and turns toxic if eaten raw or undercooked. What fungus is this?
Morchella is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).

First arising in wormlike creatures some 550 million years ago, this body-wide network coordinates actions and relays sensory signals through a central half and a peripheral half — what system is being described?
Nervous system is the highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body.

This branch of medicine focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer, a disease first documented in Egypt as early as 3000 BCE in the Edwin Smith papyrus — what is this medical specialty called?
Oncology is a branch of medicine that deals with the study, treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of cancer.
Designed by Niklaus Wirth to encourage structured programming and named after a French mathematician-philosopher, this language was developed in the pattern of ALGOL 60 — name it?

Pascal (programming language) is an imperative and procedural programming language, designed by Niklaus Wirth as a small, efficient language intended to encourage good programming practices using structured programming and data structuring.

Associated with the early 20th century, this philosophical movement tries to objectively describe subjective conscious experience exactly as it appears, without assuming anything about the outside world — which movement?
Phenomenology (philosophy) is a philosophical study and movement largely associated with the early 20th century that seeks to objectively investigate the nature of subjective, conscious experience.

It plays out everywhere from the clans of traditional societies up through modern governments, and its practitioners negotiate, make laws, and sometimes wage war; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics is the activity of settling affairs in an organized society. Politics is usually concerned with resolving issues within a society via a government.
This Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium selectively blocks antibiotics from crossing its outer membrane, making it a notorious cause of hospital-acquired pneumonia — what is it?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common encapsulated, Gram-negative, aerobic-facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that can cause disease in plants and animals, including humans.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?
One of the world's oldest crops, this thistle-like annual plant with globular orange or red flower heads is grown commercially today for oil pressed from its seeds — what is it?
Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
Applied practically by Archimedes for the quadrature of a parabola, what do we call the addition of infinitely many terms, one after another, central to calculus?
Series (mathematics) is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Which genus of about 28 grass species includes one member grown worldwide both as a cereal grain for human consumption and as fodder for livestock?
Sorghum (genus) is a genus of about 28 species of flowering plants in the grass family (Poaceae).
This towering perennial grass, native to New Guinea, stores so much natural sweetness in its jointed stalks that it's the world's primary source for a common sweetener — what plant is it?
Sugarcane is a species of tall, perennial grass (in the genus Saccharum, tribe Andropogoneae) that is used for sugar production.

Named for the order of fish that includes pufferfish, this potent neurotoxin also turns up in blue-ringed octopuses and rough-skinned newts, and is actually produced by symbiotic bacteria rather than the animals themselves — what's the toxin?

Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is a potent neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.

This American businessman co-founded and served as CEO of a ride-hailing company from 2010 to 2017, resigning amid harassment allegations, and now runs a ghost-kitchen operator called CloudKitchens — who is he?
Travis Kalanick (born August 6, 1976) is an American businessman best known as the co-founder and former chief executive officer (CEO) of Uber.
Native only to the wetlands of the Carolinas, which carnivorous plant snaps shut a 'jaw' formed from the tips of its leaves when an insect trips it?
Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) is a carnivorous plant native to the temperate and subtropical wetlands of North Carolina and South Carolina, on the East Coast of the United States.
This noble gas, found in trace amounts in Earth's atmosphere, powers arc lamps, serves as a rare anesthetic, and was the first of its family coaxed into a genuine chemical compound — which element?
Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
Often called the father of theoretical computer science, this Englishman gave us a famous 'machine' that formalized the very idea of computation — who was he?

Nicknamed 'lazy eye,' this childhood vision disorder occurs when the brain favors one eye over the other, and correcting the underlying cause doesn't restore sight right away — what is this condition?
Amblyopia: Failure of the brain to process input from one eye.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.
This British mathematician and logician coined the phrase 'mathematical induction' and gave his name to a pair of laws relating conjunction, disjunction, and negation. Who was he?
Augustus De Morgan: British mathematician and logician (1806–1871)
In continuous production since 1974 — the longest run of any civilian turboprop plane in its class — this twin-engine model also serves in medevac and flight-inspection roles — what is it?
Beechcraft Super King Air: Light twin-turboprop transport aircraft family.
Recognizable by its angled wings and forked tail, this scavenging bird of prey is thought to be the world's most abundant raptor, with a global population topping six million — which bird?
Black kite: Species of bird. The black kite or fire kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.
Named for the 18th-century French explorer who documented it on one of his expeditions, this thorny ornamental vine produces colorful bracts around three small waxy flowers — which plant is it?
First proposed after the 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese, this psychological theory says people are less likely to help a victim when others are present — what's it called?
Bystander effect: Social psychological theory. Recent research has focused on "real world" events captured on security cameras, and the coherency and robustness of the effect has come under question.

This polyatomic ion, CO3 with a 2- charge, is dissolved into water under pressure to make it fizzy, and also makes up much of the sedimentary rock in the Earth's crust — what's the ion (and salt) called?
Carbonate: Salt or ester of carbonic acid.
Discovered in 1945 and first sold in 1964, this class of beta-lactam antibiotics was originally pulled from a fungus once known as Cephalosporium — what's the family called?
Made in the skin after sun exposure and also known as vitamin D3, this compound is converted by the liver and kidneys into forms that help the body absorb calcium. What is it?

Cholecalciferol: Vitamin D3, a chemical compound. Cholecalciferol, also known as vitamin D3, colecalciferol or calciol, is a skin-made vitamin D that is found in certain foods and used as a dietary supplement.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758 and introduced to North America to control aphids, this red beetle with seven black spots gets its genus name from the Latin word for 'scarlet' — which species?
Coccinella septempunctata: Species of beetle. It inhabits many regions with a temperate climate.
This mathematical framework assigns one or more numbers to each point in space so its exact position can be pinned down — the foundation of analytic geometry. What is it called?
Coordinate system: Method for specifying point positions.

First described by Linnaeus in 1767, this citrus-family plant native to the Indian subcontinent has aromatic leaves essential to South Asian cooking, especially in India and Sri Lanka — which species?

Curry tree: Species of flowering plant. It is native to the Indian subcontinent, southern China and mainland Southeast Asia, and it has been introduced to other parts of southeast Asia and to Australia.
Nicknamed the 'gympie-gympie' by Queensland's Gubbi Gubbi people, this Australian and Malaysian rainforest plant delivers an infamously painful, long-lasting sting. What species is it?
Dendrocnide moroides: Species of plant in the nettle family.
A Canadian optical physicist at Waterloo, she shared the 2018 Nobel in Physics for the practical implementation of chirped pulse amplification — who is she?
Donna Strickland: Canadian physicist, engineer, and Nobel laureate.
Credited as the first to create a transuranium element — neptunium — this Berkeley physicist shared the 1951 Nobel in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Also called Human Factors Engineering, this discipline applies psychology and physiology to reduce errors and boost safety in system design — what field?
Ergonomics: Designing systems to suit their users.
One of only two living species in its genus, this rodent was such a prized delicacy to the ancient Romans that its common name literally advertises the fact. What animal is it?
European edible dormouse: Species of rodent.

Marked by widespread chronic pain plus fatigue and foggy thinking, this condition affects 2 to 4% of people, more often women, and was first recognised in the 1950s but only defined in 1990 — what is it?
Dubbed the "Flying Tailor," this inventor was so sure his wearable parachute would work that he leapt from the Eiffel Tower to test it himself — fatally. Who was he?
What is this — “Sexually transmitted infection caused by certain types of human papillomaviruses”?
Genital wart: Sexually transmitted infection caused by certain types of human papillomaviruses. Warts are the most easily recognized symptom of genital HPV infection.

Identified in 1898 by an Italian pathologist and later named in his honor, this cell organelle packages proteins into vesicles and adds sugar chains before shipping them to their destination. What is it called?
Golgi apparatus: Cell organelle that packages proteins for export.
A lentivirus and member of the retrovirus family, it gradually cripples the human immune system — and untreated, leaves roughly 9 to 11 years before the immune collapse called AIDS. What is it?
HIV: Human retrovirus, cause of AIDS. Without treatment, the average survival time after infection with HIV is estimated to be 9 to 11 years, depending on the HIV subtype.
This Michigan farm boy left home at 16 for Detroit, later patented the Model T's transmission, and gave his name to a whole system of mass production. Who was he?
This British Egyptologist discovered the untouched tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings in November 1922 — who is he?
Howard Carter: British archaeologist and Egyptologist (1874–1939)
Distinguished by the male's large, transversely ridged curved horns, which wild goat species roams Eurasia and Africa?
This order of crustaceans includes both seafaring gribbles and the woodlice in your garden, with females brooding their young in a belly pouch called a marsupium. What is it?
Isopoda: Order of arthropods. The order is divided into eleven suborders.
As Grand Pensionary of Holland during the Dutch Golden Age, this statesman dominated politics from 1650 until the 'Disaster Year' of 1672 — who was he?
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years fighting skepticism over messenger RNA before her groundwork made mRNA vaccines possible, earning a shared 2023 Nobel Prize — who is she?
He co-founded a certain search company with Sergey Brin, later led its parent Alphabet as CEO, and is now among the two wealthiest people on Earth — who is it?
Sometimes called the paleomammalian cortex, this set of brain structures — including the amygdala — governs emotion, motivation, and long-term memory — what is it called?
Limbic system: Set of brain structures involved in emotion and motivation. Its various components support a variety of functions including emotion, behavior, long-term memory, and olfaction.

This German fluid dynamicist built the mathematical foundations of subsonic aerodynamics, identifying the 'boundary layer' and lifting-line theory — and lent his name to a dimensionless number. Who was he?

First isolated in the 1770s and carrying atomic number 25, this hard, silvery transition metal is a key alloying agent in stainless steel and also an essential trace nutrient in the human diet — which element?
Manganese: Chemical element with atomic number 25 (Mn)

Co-inventor of a heart-valve repair device called the MitraClip, this Turkish-American cardiac surgeon became a famous TV health personality before being named the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in 2025 — who is he?
Mehmet Oz: American TV host and government official (born 1960)
Sold as Versed, this benzodiazepine sedates rather than knocks you out, can be sprayed up the nose or squirted in the cheek, and famously causes anterograde amnesia — which drug?
Midazolam: Benzodiazepine used for anesthesia and procedural sedation.
First prepared in 1908 by biochemist Kikunae Ikeda as he tried to bottle the savory taste of kombu seaweed, this flavor enhancer is the original source of umami in cooking — what is it?
Monosodium glutamate: Flavor enhancer (621 or E621)

This inner-ear condition brings on episodes of vertigo, ringing in the ears, and hearing loss lasting anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours — believed to stem from fluid buildup in the labyrinth. What is it?
Ménière's disease: Disorder of the inner ear. The hearing loss and ringing in the ears can become constant over time.
Its name literally means 'blue cow,' though only the males actually sport a bluish-grey coat — which is the largest antelope species in Asia?
Starting as a metals trader after the Soviet Union's collapse, which Russian billionaire built the Sayanogorsk smelter into the world's largest aluminium company, Rusal?
Created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993, this scripting language's name began as 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym meaning 'Hypertext Preprocessor' — what is it?
PHP: Scripting language created in 1994. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Nicknamed "javelina" or "skunk pig," this social New World mammal travels in herds called squadrons and counts true pigs as its closest living relatives — what pig-like ungulate is it?
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive fear that persists more than six months and can trigger fainting in blood-or-injury cases — what is it?
Phobia: Anxiety disorder classified by a persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Downgraded from planet to dwarf in 2006 when astronomers adopted a new definition, this Kuiper belt object orbits beyond Neptune—what celestial body is it?
Pluto: Largest dwarf planet. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).
Once one of America's leading rocket experts with an MIT aeronautics degree, he was deported to China in 1955 and went on to father that nation's space program — which aerospace engineer?

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.
Known by the E number E211, this white crystalline salt of benzoic acid is a widely used food preservative and pickling agent — what is it?
Sodium benzoate: Common food preservative. It appears as a white crystalline chemical with the formula C6H5COONa.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
